Kalp Mehta Mahindra Finance Internship Experience. 
The Mahindra Finance Summer Internship process began with an iniƟal resume shortlisƟng 
round, followed by two rounds — an apƟtude test and a coding assessment. 
OA: Round 1 – ApƟtude Test (25/11/25) 
The test included quesƟons from: 
 
General English – mainly comprehension and grammar 
 
QuanƟtaƟve ApƟtude – basic arithmeƟc, percentages, and logical reasoning 
 
AnalyƟcal Thinking 
Overall, the diﬃculty level was easy. The focus was more on speed and accuracy rather than 
advanced concepts. 
Round 2 – Coding Assessment (26/11/25) 
Candidates who cleared the apƟtude round were shortlisted for the online coding 
assessment, conducted the very next day. 
This round had two secƟons: 
1. Python MCQs (20 quesƟons, 15–20 minutes) – Covering topics like loops, funcƟons, 
data types, and error handling. 
2. Coding Problems (3 quesƟons) – Only Python was allowed. 
The coding problems were simple and logic-based. I was able to solve all three within the 
given Ɵme and ensured that my code was clean and readable. 
 
Pre-Interview Session (PPT) (28/11/25) 
On 28th November, Mahindra Finance conducted an oﬄine PPT on campus. 
I would strongly recommend aƩending this session seriously, as it gives you a clear 
understanding of: 
 
The company’s core operaƟons and values 
 
The kind of skills and mindset they expect from interns 
It’s also a very good opportunity to ask thoughƞul and relevant quesƟons. One thing I 
personally noƟced was that the students who showed genuine interest and asked good 
quesƟons were being observed. Since this was our ﬁrst PPT for Mahindra Finance, we 
weren’t fully aware of how important that could be for us.

Interview Day – 29th November 2025 
The interviews were scheduled oﬄine, and candidates were given the opƟon to choose 
between two roles one day prior: 
 
IT Role 
 
Data Analyst Role 
I chose the IT role. Out of 20 shortlisted candidates, 8 opted for IT and 12 for Data Analyst. 
Round 1 – Technical Interview 
My technical interview was scheduled 5th in order started around 11:45 am and lasted 
around 35–40 minutes. 
The interviewer began by asking for a brief introducƟon. I gave a short and structured 
overview menƟoning my branch, minor, key interests, and 1–2 important projects I had 
worked on. I would suggest not memorizing a ﬁxed introducƟon. Instead, be clear about 
what you want to include and present it naturally. 
This introducƟon actually set the tone for the rest of the interview. Since I menƟoned 
projects like QRLY and NEP Timetable Generator, she asked me to explain one of them in 
depth starƟng from the idea behind it to how I implemented it. 
We discussed why I chose speciﬁc tech stacks and how I integrated the diﬀerent 
components. I realized they were not just evaluaƟng technical skills, but also how clearly I 
could think and communicate my approach. 
One important thing  know your projects inside out. Be clear about: 
 
The real-world problem it solves 
 
The use case 
 
Why you chose a parƟcular approach 
 
How it connects to the job descripƟon 
For example, the job role involved data collecƟon and analysis, and my QRLY project aligned 
well with that. That alignment deﬁnitely worked in my favor. 
AŌer the project discussion, she moved to SQL. I was asked to write and explain queries such 
as: 
 
Create, Alter, delete, and replace queries 
 
Diﬀerence between DELETE and TRUNCATE 
 
Finding the 3rd highest salary from an employee table (in two diﬀerent ways)

I explained both the syntax and the reasoning behind each query. It’s important to 
understand that they are not just tesƟng memorizaƟon  they want to see whether you truly 
understand what each command does. For example, I didn’t remember the exact syntax of 
the ALTER command , but my concept was clear and I was close to the soluƟon. That clarity 
maƩers more than word-to-word accuracy. 
Next, she asked a conceptual quesƟon from OperaƟng Systems about MulƟthreading. I 
explained how mulƟple threads run concurrently to improve performance, and brieﬂy 
discussed synchronizaƟon and some scheduling concepts. We discussed working of diﬀerent 
scheduling algorithms also menƟoned one of the algorithms which I have used in my one of 
the project at backend for load balancing. How it works pracƟcally and etc. 
Then came a situaƟon-based quesƟon aligned with the IT role. She presented a real-world 
scenario: 
“Let’s say the UPI organizaƟon introduces new features and funcƟonaliƟes. What measures 
would you take before integraƟng them into the Mahindra Finance system?” 
I approached it step by step ﬁrst understanding the requirements, then considering security 
implicaƟons, backward compaƟbility, system impact analysis, tesƟng in a staging 
environment, and ensuring proper validaƟon before deployment. I tried to structure my 
answer logically rather than jumping straight to a technical soluƟon. 
Towards the end, she asked some behavioral and company-related quesƟons, such as: 
 
“Why do you want to join Mahindra Finance?” 
 
“What interests you about this role?” 
Since I had paid aƩenƟon during the PPT and done some research, I connected my answers 
to their digital iniƟaƟves and my interest in working on scalable, data-driven systems. 
Finally, I asked two thoughƞul quesƟons one about Mahindra Finance’s future scope in 
digiƟzaƟon and another about one  related to  the recent news of company . She 
appreciated the curiosity, and we had a meaningful two-way discussion. 
The interview ended on a very posiƟve note. It felt more like a professional conversaƟon 
than a strict Q&A session. 
One key thing to remember: during the interview, stay aƩenƟve and try to align yourself 
with the job descripƟon. Understand what problem they are trying to solve and posiƟon 
yourself as someone who can contribute to that soluƟon. 
Post-Interview Thoughts 
Walking out of the interview room, I felt saƟsﬁed. It wasn’t perfect, but it was genuine — a 
mix of learning, clarity, and conﬁdence. A few hours later, I received the message that I had 
been shortlisted for the HR round.

Looking back, the key takeaway from this round is simple: 
“Know your resume deeply, understand your projects inside-out, and express your thoughts 
clearly. They’re not looking for perfecƟon — they’re looking for potenƟal.” 
 
Round 2 – HR Interview 
AŌer the technical interviews concluded, a total of 8 candidates were shortlisted for the HR 
round 4 from the IT role and 4 from the DnA (Data & AnalyƟcs) role. 
To be honest, I was slightly more nervous for this round, because I hadn’t had much Ɵme to 
speciﬁcally prepare for HR-style quesƟons. Most of my preparaƟon Ɵme had gone into 
technical topics. So instead of overthinking, I decided to just be myself and keep the 
conversaƟon as natural as possible. And honestly, that approach worked well. 
StarƟng the ConversaƟon 
The HR greeted me warmly and, aŌer a brief exchange of greeƟngs, asked: 
“Give a brief introducƟon about yourself from childhood to where you are today.” 
I took a moment to organize my thoughts and then narrated my journey in a story-like 
format  starƟng from my early educaƟon, how I developed curiosity for technology, and how 
that gradually led me to pursue Electronics & TelecommunicaƟon Engineering at VJTI. 
I also spoke about how my interest in soŌware development evolved over Ɵme and how 
working on projects and in teams helped me build problem-solving skills and handle 
deadlines. 
I ended by menƟoning a few hobbies and personal qualiƟes that reﬂect how I approach 
work being analyƟcal, consistent, and comfortable in collaboraƟve environments. 
For this part, just be genuine. And wherever possible, subtly highlight qualiƟes like 
leadership, adaptability, Ɵme management, and teamwork through your journey rather than 
directly claiming them. 
The Puzzle QuesƟon 
Next, he gave me a small puzzle quesƟon. I hadn’t speciﬁcally prepared puzzles, but I tried to 
think calmly and solve it logically during the conversaƟon. 
If I could give one suggesƟon here pracƟce a few common puzzles beforehand from 
plaƞorms like GeeksforGeeks. They’re usually not very diﬃcult. The goal is to see how you 
think aloud, structure your reasoning, and stay composed under pressure.

SituaƟon-Based and Behavioral QuesƟons 
AŌer that, the HR moved to a few situaƟon-based quesƟons, which are quite common in HR 
rounds. 
For example: 
 
“If a teammate suddenly leaves in the middle of a project, how would you handle it?” 
 
“If your manager has a diﬀerent approach to a task than yours, how would you deal 
with it?” 
For such quesƟons, I focused on giving balanced and pracƟcal answers. 
I explained that I would ﬁrst understand the other person’s perspecƟve, communicate my 
suggesƟons respecƞully, and then align with the ﬁnal team decision keeping a learning 
mindset and prioriƟzing the overall project’s success. 
For the team scenario, I shared an example from one of my college projects where we 
managed workload distribuƟon, handled last-minute issues, and maintained coordinaƟon 
even under pressure. 
The key takeaway here is: 
Always frame your answers to reﬂect teamwork, adaptability, ownership, and problem-
solving. 
Avoid rigid responses like “I’ll just follow the manager blindly.” Instead, show that you 
respect hierarchy but can also think criƟcally and communicate eﬀecƟvely. 
QuesƟons to the HR (The Most Important Part) 
Towards the end which I personally feel was the strongest part of the enƟre interview the HR 
asked if I had any quesƟons for him. 
Many candidates underesƟmate this moment, but it’s actually a great opportunity to leave a 
lasƟng impression. 
Based on my prior research about Mahindra Finance and its iniƟaƟves, I asked a couple of 
thoughƞul quesƟons related to their digital transformaƟon journey and how technology is 
shaping their operaƟons. These weren’t generic quesƟons, but more strategic and forward-
looking. He appreciated the depth and menƟoned that it reﬂected genuine interest. 
I then asked about his personal experience at Mahindra Finance. His answer was very 
passionate he spoke about the culture, ownership, innovaƟon, and what makes the 
organizaƟon stand out from an employee’s perspecƟve. 
I wrapped up by connecƟng his response with my own interest in working at a place that 
combines technology with meaningful real-world impact, especially at the common man’s

level. That made the ending feel very natural and engaging more like a conversaƟon than an 
interview. 
 
The Result 
On 2nd December 2025,the ﬁnal results were announced ,and I was selected. 
Looking back, this achievement was not just mine. It was built on the constant support and 
encouragement of my seniors, friends, and family. I am truly grateful to everyone who 
guided and stood by me throughout this journey.
